newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks restrained by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks restrained by profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed marginally lower for the first time in over three weeks as small investors took profit in selected stocks, while blue chip foreign buying supported turnover, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.97 points lower at 629.83, after rising steadily from 597.50 points on October 28.
Price declines led gains by 20 to 30. Development Finance fell four rupees to 286, Agalawatte Plantations 6.25 to 27.
"Retail investors took profits, but the decline is temporary because they will return to the market in a day or two," said Grodon Nadesan a trader at brokerage CT Smith.

Brokers said retail investor sentiment was hit by Tuesday's offer by Asia Capital to buy Vanik. "It caused concern among investors who cold not understand what was happening," said Nouzab Fareed, general manager of Allied Phillips Securities.
Investment bank Asia Capital made an offer to buy investment bank Vanik, on the basis of 10 rupees in cash and one new share of Asia Capital. Vanik has yet to respond to the take-over bid.
Turnover was 57.41 million rupees on 870,174 shares, supported by foreign buying of 234,700 blue chip John Keells Holdings at 190 rupees, four rupees up.
"Foreign buyers will pay premiums for a quantity of a blue chips," said CT Smith's Nadesan. --Prithi kodagoda (941) 434319
